verse: but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in human likeness.
story: Paul quotes what is probably an early hymn about Christ, and the turning point is a single verb: emptied.

The One who shared the form of God did not lose His deity; He set aside the privileges of display and took the form of a servant. He was made in human likeness, a real body, hunger, tiredness and all. Paul is not offering a puzzle to solve. He is holding up the pattern for a community: the Lord of all chose the lowest place for the sake of others.
When you are tempted to insist on your own way today, look at Him. Humility is not weakness, but the shape of Christ.
